@graph.name: Do I need an Esker alternative to add spoken orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Esker carries on with whatever arrives in your inbox: capturing and checking it, then the credit checks and cash collection that follow. What we add happens before an order gets to Esker: for each restaurant you move off the phone, its chef names the items aloud in our app and checks the list before it goes.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Esker?

acceptedAnswer.text: At one job: getting a restaurant's order from the chef to you with nobody on the phone, looked over by whoever knows what the kitchen is low on. Esker covers far more ground than we do, from capture to cash, so we work next to it rather than as an Esker alternative.

@graph.name: Esker's capture page is written for customers who send orders any way they like. Why change how restaurants order?

acceptedAnswer.text: Its idea is to let customers send orders as they like, then read them as they come in. It suits trade customers who email or fax their own order forms. Phoned orders give Esker nothing to read: someone on your side writes them down first. Our app changes only that habit, and only for the restaurants you put on it.

@graph.name: Is the app linked to Esker, and will our order desk still have to type orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No link is built in: they come from separate companies, and neither supports the other's software. Over EDI or our API, if your ERP accepts orders that way, nobody retypes them; we confirm that in the demo. By email, you get a PDF, Excel or Word file. Esker is built to read emailed orders, so ask Esker whether your setup can handle ours: we have not built anything for it, so we promise nothing. If it cannot, your staff type the file in. Even so, nobody has to pick up a call, jot it down and repeat it back, because the chef cleared each item before it was sent. A chef can still miss a mistake or change their mind afterwards, so an order can still be wrong. Your ERP holds accounts, invoices and stock on file; we hold a guide for each restaurant with its prices, and a copy of the orders chefs send in the app.

@graph.name: Esker already has a customer portal with an AI agent. Isn't that enough?

acceptedAnswer.text: For customers who will log in and type, it may be. Esker's portal takes orders at any hour, and its AI agent helps customers find products and order there, so keep it for them. We built our app for the chef who would rather pick up the phone: they speak the items, see the list and fix a wrong one before sending.

@graph.name: Esker runs credit checks before we invoice. Do app orders get them too?

acceptedAnswer.text: That depends on where your credit checks run and how our order gets into your ERP. Ask Esker which of its checks would apply to an order your people type into the ERP, or to one arriving by EDI or the API. Nothing we offer sends our orders through Esker. Once it sits in your ERP as an order, billing, collections and payments that run from it treat it like any other.

@graph.name: How soon could we be live, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Setup takes 24 to 48 hours for most distributors, with no changes made to Esker. You share what each restaurant usually orders, often as a spreadsheet from your ERP. We load those lists, set each restaurant up, and its chef installs our app; most are ordering the same day. Esker gives each customer a quote rather than a public price, which is how we price for distributors as well. An Esker replacement means moving order capture, billing and collections onto new software; adding our ordering app next to Esker leaves that work where it is.

@graph.name: Where do the Esker details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: From esker.com as it was on 9 November 2026: the homepage, its pages on order management, order data capture, AI agents, deductions, industries and fax, its overview of the order-to-cash suite, the solution summary for order management, and two food customer stories (Suntory Beverage & Food Spain and Paulig). We also searched for voice or phone ordering tools made for Esker and found none. Seen something that has changed? Tell us and we will fix it.
